Weighted Cross-Tabulation for Two Discrete Variables (Multiply-Imputed SCF)

Source: R/scf_xtab.R
scf_xtab.Rd

Computes a weighted cross-tabulation between two categorical variables in multiply-imputed SCF data using Rubin's Rules. Returns national population counts and percent breakdowns by cell, row, or column.

scf_xtab(design, rowvar, colvar, percent = "cell", max_cats = 20)

Arguments

design

A multiply-imputed svrepdesign object created with scf_load().

rowvar

A one-sided formula specifying the row variable, e.g., ~edcl.

colvar

A one-sided formula specifying the column variable, e.g., ~racecl.

percent

Character. Choose how to scale percentages:

  • "cell" (default): proportion of total population

  • "row": proportion within each row group

  • "col": proportion within each column group

max_cats

Maximum allowed categories in either variable (default: 20).

Value

A data.frame with the following columns:

  • row: Row category label

  • col: Column category label

  • count: Estimated national count for that cell

  • percent: Weighted proportion, scaled by the selected percent argument (0 to 1)

The "implicates" attribute contains the list of implicate-specific svytable objects.

See also

svytable(), scf_plot_bbar(), scf_freq()
